**RE: Urgent Prior Authorization Appeal**
*   **Member Name:** Harper Hayes
*   **Member ID:** W668248955
*   **Plan:** Tufts Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), State of Rhode Island
*   **Reference Number:** POC-E8E7B452F1-10979
*   **Requested Service:** Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)
*   **Provider:** Dr. Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeals and Grievances Department,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of coverage for the arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) scheduled by my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD. The denial letter dated August 15, 2026, states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." 

This determination is incorrect and directly contradicted by my medical records. My clinical history fully satisfies and exceeds the conservative treatment requirements outlined in Tufts Health Plan's governing medical policy: **Evolent Clinical Guideline 1770 for Shoulder Arthroscopy** (formerly National Imaging Associates, Inc. Clinical Guidelines: Shoulder Arthroscopy, Guideline Number **Evolent_CG_1770** / **NIA_CG_318**). 

### 1. Clinical Summary and Diagnostic Findings
My MRI scan dated July 9, 2026, reveals a **1.8 cm full-thickness supraspinatus tear** with grade 2 fatty atrophy. This placing my injury squarely under the policy section: **"Medium (1-3 cm) or Large (3-5 cm), Full-Thickness Rotator Cuff Tear"**.

According to the policy, a "Surgical repair of a medium or large full-thickness rotator cuff tear may be necessary when" certain criteria are met, specifically:
> **"When ALL of the following criteria are met:"**
> *   **"Reproducible rotator cuff pain patterns (lateral arm, deltoid pain not radiating past the elbow, night pain, or pain with overhead motions)"**
> *   **"Functional loss (age-appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs), occupational, or athletic)"**
> *   **"Positive impingement signs and/or tests on exam (Hawkins, Neer, Jobe test or reproducible pain when arm is positioned overhead (above plane of shoulder) with relief of pain when arm is repositioned below the plane of the shoulder)"**

My clinical records clearly document that I meet every single one of these criteria:
*   **Pain Patterns:** I have suffered from 12 months of progressive, severe shoulder pain, including unremitting night pain that prevents me from sleeping on my affected side, and sharp pain with overhead movements.
*   **Functional Loss:** I experience severe, disabling functional limitations. I am unable to lift my arm above shoulder height, which severely limits my basic activities of daily living (ADLs).
*   **Physical Exam:** Dr. Marchetti’s physical examination documented positive provocative testing (including positive impingement signs) on the affected side, and my range of motion is significantly limited by pain.

### 2. Refutation of the Denial: Complete Exhaustion of Conservative Treatment
Even though some policies waive conservative care for full-thickness tears depending on the patient's age and acute trauma status, my records document that I have already completed a comprehensive and exhaustive trial of non-operative care. 

The policy defines "Non-operative management" as follows:
> **"Non-operative management, when required, will be specified within the clinical indications below and may include one or more of the following:**
> \u25cf **Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program**
> \u25cf **Rest or activity modification**
> \u25cf **Application of heat or ice**
> \u25cf **Minimum of 4 weeks of oral NSAIDs (if not medically contraindicated)**
> \u25cf **Single injection of corticosteroid and local anesthetic into subacromial, intra-articular space, or bicipital groove"**

My medical records confirm that I have tried and failed **every single one** of these conservative modalities:
1.  **Supervised Physical Therapy:** I completed **8 weeks (24 full sessions)** of supervised physical therapy from May 8, 2026, to July 3, 2026, focusing on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics. Despite 100% compliance, my pain and range of motion did not improve. This is fully documented in my attached physical therapy discharge note. This trial far exceeds the standard "failure of at least 6 weeks of non-operative treatment*, including physical therapy" applied to smaller tears under the same guideline.
2.  **Oral Medications:** I have been taking oral NSAIDs for **6 months** with inadequate pain relief, exceeding the "Minimum of 4 weeks of oral NSAIDs" guideline.
3.  **Corticosteroid Injection:** I received a "Single injection of corticosteroid and local anesthetic" on May 13, 2026. This provided only 4 weeks of temporary, partial relief before my pain returned to baseline.
4.  **Rest and Activity Modification:** I have experienced 12 months of progressive pain that remains completely unrelieved by rest and activity modification.

### 3. General Requirements Met
Furthermore, I meet all "GENERAL REQUIREMENTS" for elective shoulder surgery under the policy:
*   I have no active local or systemic infection.
*   I have no active, untreated drug dependency.
*   I am a non-smoker.
*   My BMI is 29, meaning I am not excluded due to "an excessively high BMI" and my health is optimized for surgery.

### Conclusion
My 1.8 cm full-thickness rotator cuff tear is highly symptomatic, causing severe functional impairment, and has failed to respond to 8 weeks of intensive physical therapy, 6 months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection. Delaying this surgery further risks muscle retraction and irreversible fatty degeneration (which is already at Grade 2).

Please review the attached physical therapy discharge summary, MRI report, and Dr. Marchetti's clinical notes, and reverse this denial immediately so that I can proceed with this medically necessary surgery.

Sincerely,

Harper Hayes
